design.chosen: a byte-pinned engine-Y copy of the O-ext unit runner plus two engine-Y settings files, packed on engine Y's pack under the names the job runner calls and seals; oext_eval.py (every O-ext rule) is engine X's file on both engines
design.why_not_settings_only: engine X's oext_unit.py loads settings/oext_unit.json by its literal SETTINGS_SHA256 3959eae7 and oext_eval.json by oext_eval.py's literal 2ad98938, and s1common.check_settings refuses a settings file whose engine_x is not the running engine; so Y settings at those paths with X's runner refuse on the pod, while check-plan (presence only) would pass them: a pod-side crash after the paid setup. Measured: the bundle test's X-files layout on engine Y refuses 'settings oext_unit: written for engine 472fc7f6..., this engine is 34bfd288...'.
design.why_not_per_engine_section: oext_unit.py's validate_settings fixes the key set and one engine_x; a per-engine section needs a code change to an X-side file (forbidden: block A's outputs name it by SHA-256).
design.why_not_runner_change: a job-runner change (Y hosts call oext_unit_y.py and seal its own settings names) would avoid the pack-time renames, but job_runner_stage1.py is outside this brief's files, and X's validate_settings would still force oext.settings.path to name settings/oext_eval.json; offered as an alternative (open point 2).
design.why_not_thin_wrapper: a wrapper calling oext_unit.main(settings=..., oext_settings=...) must sit at the runner's path, so engine X's oext_unit.py would have to be packed under another name; main documents those arguments as test fixtures only.
design.allowed_recipes_on_y: B+Qi only (37942cf5, plan.json recipes_y; computed by engine Y's code from Y's tree, M). B, S and G stay on engine X with oext_unit.json (§34 point 1). The generation and guard pins are engine X's (B+Qi's blocks hash to them on engine Y, M), so one cap and one judge.
